title: Being a Physics Student
pedagogicalStatus: Unreviewed author draft; formative practice only

sources.title: Meet Maya — a Student Profile
paragraphs: My name is Maya Brooks, and I am a first-year physics student at North Valley College. I am nineteen years old. I live near the campus with my sister. My sister studies chemistry, but I study physics. We often walk to college together.

My classes start at nine o'clock on Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. On Wednesday, my first class starts at ten. I have a mathematics class on Monday morning and an introductory physics class on Tuesday morning. We have a laboratory session on Thursday afternoon.
Our physics instructor is Ms. Reed. She explains new words before every activity. I do not always understand the instructions the first time, so I sometimes ask her to repeat a sentence.
After class, I usually review my notes at the library. On Friday, I study at home. I want to understand physics and communicate clearly in English.

sources.title: Two Students in One Class
paragraphs: Daniel is a second-year physics student. He lives in a small apartment and takes the bus to campus. On Tuesdays, he meets his study group in the library.

His classmate Lina is also a physics student. She usually walks to university. She has a laboratory session on Mondays, but not on Fridays. She enjoys reading short articles about stars. Daniel prefers experiments about motion.
They attend the same English workshop. They work together on Wednesday afternoons and help each other with physics vocabulary.

sources.title: Physics Department — Welcome Session
paragraphs: Monday, 9:00 a.m.: Meet your class in Room 12.
Monday, 10:15 a.m.: Visit the science library.
Tuesday, 11:00 a.m.: Introductory physics lecture in Hall B.
Thursday, 2:00 p.m.: Laboratory introduction in Lab 3.
Bring your student card and a notebook. You do not need laboratory equipment for the welcome session.

sources.title: An Academic Email (fictional)
paragraphs: To: course.assistant@example.org. Subject: Question about the laboratory introduction.
My name is Jordan Lee, and I am a new physics student. Does Thursday's laboratory introduction start at 2:00 p.m.? Is it in Lab 3?
The address in this teaching example is fictional. Please do not send messages to it.

items.prompt: Complete: I ___ a physics student.
items.feedback: Use am with I.

items.prompt: Complete: She ___ in our physics class.
items.feedback: A singular third-person subject takes is.

items.prompt: Complete: They ___ first-year students.
items.feedback: They takes are in the present.

items.prompt: Choose the correct negative statement.
items.feedback: Put not after the verb is.

items.prompt: Choose the correct question.
items.feedback: A yes/no question with be begins with is, are or am.

items.prompt: Complete: ___ they in Lab 3?
items.feedback: Put are before they to ask about location.

items.prompt: Complete: Are you ready? Yes, I ___.
items.feedback: Use Yes, I am to answer Are you...?

items.prompt: Complete: I ___ a scientific calculator.
items.feedback: Use have with I.

items.prompt: Complete: Daniel ___ a notebook.
items.feedback: Third-person singular usually takes has.

items.prompt: Complete: ___ you have a physics class today?
items.feedback: Use Do you have...? to ask a present-simple question.

items.prompt: Complete: Maya ___ her notes after class. (review)
items.feedback: In the present simple, add -s with she or Maya.

items.prompt: Complete: Daniel ___ the bus to campus. (take)
items.feedback: Use takes for a regular routine with Daniel.

items.prompt: Complete: Lina ___ have a lab on Friday.
items.feedback: Use doesn't + base verb with she or Lina.

items.prompt: Choose the word that means 'on most days'.
items.feedback: Usually describes something that happens regularly.

items.prompt: Complete: ___ you study physics?
items.feedback: Do starts a present-simple yes/no question with you.

items.prompt: Choose the correct question.
items.feedback: Use where + does + subject + base verb.

items.prompt: Choose the correct question about a place.
items.feedback: Use Where is...? to ask where a place is.

items.prompt: What is a notebook used for in class?
items.feedback: A notebook is used for writing or recording notes.

items.prompt: What is a lecture?
items.feedback: A lecture is an instructional presentation.

items.prompt: Choose the natural phrase.
items.feedback: Attend a lecture is the natural collocation.

items.prompt: Complete: Please ___ notes during the explanation.
items.feedback: Take notes is the usual collocation.

items.prompt: What subject does Maya study?
items.feedback: Maya says that she studies physics.

items.prompt: Who studies chemistry?
items.feedback: The passage says that Maya's sister studies chemistry.

items.prompt: On which day is Maya's laboratory session?
items.feedback: Maya describes a laboratory session on Thursday afternoon.

items.prompt: At what time does Maya's first class begin on Wednesday?
items.feedback: Her first class on Wednesday starts at ten.

items.prompt: Where does Maya usually review her notes?
items.feedback: The last paragraph says she reviews notes at the library.

items.prompt: How does Daniel travel to campus?
items.feedback: Daniel takes the bus to campus.

items.prompt: When do Daniel and Lina work together?
items.feedback: The text says Wednesday afternoons.

items.prompt: Where is the Tuesday physics lecture?
items.feedback: The Tuesday lecture is listed in Hall B.

items.prompt: What should students bring to the welcome session?
items.feedback: The welcome notice requests a student card and a notebook.

items.prompt: At what time is the Thursday laboratory introduction?
items.feedback: The Thursday introduction is scheduled for 2:00 p.m.

items.prompt: Who wrote the email?
items.feedback: The sender signs as Jordan Lee.

items.prompt: What does Jordan want to confirm?
items.feedback: Jordan asks about the laboratory time and location.

items.prompt: Which expression closes the email?
items.feedback: Best regards is the email closing.
